limitations: Source-backed conversion tests cover all 135 public IDs; this is not a claim that all 135 were pulled in a clean installed wheel with an empty cache.
An independently installed base-only wheel was tested on representative families with no checkout or standalone Python formats package. Its exact final-build results are recorded separately.
Dryad returned HTTP 429 during earlier isolated tests. The final clean-wheel guava retry succeeded after cooldown; provider rate limits remain possible.
ChEMBL preserves native peak lists instead of reconstructing an undocumented broadened representation; five inherited annotation fields absent from its SQLite source remain null.
Private datasets still require authorized protected access. No public data bytes or profiles are redistributed.

methodology.dryad_mendeley_fairdata_harvard: 21 Dryad, 16 Mendeley, 1 Fairdata and 1 Harvard Dataverse datasets

ecosis.native_cold_get: No standalone get() call began with an empty raw cache. For the single listed dataset, PullContext.download fetched the source into a fresh empty cache, then get() ran from an empty root using that just-populated cache, without staged source bytes. The native download completed in one stream; interruption and resume were covered by synthetic Rust tests.
ecosis.origin_http: Every listed recipe input was obtained from its published public origin with live HTTP into a temporary staging area. Large Cabo files required standard HTTP Range resumption after gateway interruptions; incomplete or corrupted segments were discarded before validation.
ecosis.reference_parity: The four Cabo files were compared in full against local read-only standardized reference X, every declared Y, and sample identity. The reference supplied validation only and was not an input to recipe execution.
ecosis.staged_assembly: Each dataset recipe was assembled using the downloaded origin inputs supplied to a test context, then passed through public_pull.pull, canonical conversion and NirsDataset.x(), y(), and metadata(). This staged test does not test the actual Python/native download path.

other: No dataset bytes, local paths, credentials or guestbook responses are included.
Shape and conversion claims refer to the actual upstream bytes; cached/raw-staged and clean-wheel cold tests are distinguished per record.
